guide.desc: Step by step, on a Samsung Galaxy, how to make the text on a parent's smartphone bigger: font size, screen zoom, Easy mode and accessibility settings. Plus why calling can still be hard afterwards, and what helps.
guide.faq.1.a: That is the best way. The first time the app opens you choose the language, text size and photo shape and put family members in their places. If you do that once, your parent only has to tap a card from then on. It takes five minutes on a weekend or holiday visit.
guide.faq.1.q: Can I install it on my parent's phone for them?
guide.faq.2.a: No. The phone app they already use stays exactly as it is. 88Phone sits on top of it, so if it is not for you, just uninstall it. It never edits or deletes contacts either.
guide.faq.2.q: Does the existing phone app disappear?
guide.faq.3.a: You can use it as soon as you install it. For free you get four people as big photo cards and can both call and text. There are no ads, even in the free version. If you want to add more people, you pay once. It is not a monthly fee.
guide.faq.4.a: For now it runs only on Android (Galaxy and others).
guide.h1: How to enlarge the text on a parent's phone
guide.intro: If your parent has told you "I can't read the screen", there is more you can fix in the phone's settings than you might think. Go through the steps below once. It is fastest to do it with their phone in your hands.
guide.meta: Written for Samsung Galaxy · other Android phones use slightly different menu names
guide.more: To see what 88Phone is like, visit the about page.
guide.ogDesc: Step by step on a Galaxy. What settings can do, and what they never quite fix.
guide.ogTitle: How to enlarge the text on a parent's phone
guide.s1.p1: Go to Settings → Display → Font size and style and you will find a slider at the bottom. Push it all the way to the right. On the same screen, turn on Bold font too; the letters become crisper and far easier to read.
guide.s1.p2: On a phone that is not a Galaxy, the same setting is under Settings → Display → Display size and text.
guide.s2.h2: 2. Enlarge the whole screen, not just the text
guide.s2.p1: If you only enlarge the text, buttons and icons stay small and are hard to tap. In Settings → Display → Screen zoom, move the slider to the right and buttons and pictures grow with the text. Steps 1 and 2 only really work together.
guide.s3.p1: Samsung phones have Settings → Display → Easy mode. Turn it on and the home screen icons and text get bigger all at once and the layout becomes simpler. For an older parent this alone makes a big difference.
guide.s4.l1: Settings → Accessibility → Visibility enhancements → High contrast fonts — increases the difference between text and background.
guide.s4.l2: On the same screen, turn on Magnification to zoom in on part of the screen.
guide.s4.l3: Increasing Settings → Accessibility → Interaction and dexterity → Touch and hold delay reduces accidental taps from shaky hands.
guide.s4.p1: Menu names vary a little by phone model and software version. Type "font size" into the search box at the top of Settings and it takes you straight there.
guide.s5.h2: 5. What is still a problem after all that
guide.s5.l1: With hundreds of contacts, finding a name is hard in itself. Bigger text means fewer names fit on one screen, so there is more scrolling.
guide.s5.l2: The bigger the text, the more names get cut off in the middle. When "Kim Youngsoo eldest son" shows as "Kim Youngsoo eld…", you cannot tell who it is.
guide.s5.l3: Making a call takes several taps. Phone app → Contacts → Search → Name → Call button.
guide.s5.l4: When a call was missed, only the number is left, so they do not know who called.
guide.s5.p1: Even after enlarging every setting, before long you will hear "I can't make calls" again. Small text was never the whole problem.
guide.s6.l1: Names are never cut off. The text shrinks to fit the card so the name fits on one line.
guide.s6.l2: There are five text sizes, and one card per row makes everything bigger still.
guide.s6.l3: If photos feel like too much, you can hide them and show only very large names.
guide.s6.l4: If a call was missed, that person's card blinks. A face instead of a number.
guide.s6.l5: Texts are sent without a keyboard, by choosing a sentence like "Please call me" or "Have you eaten?".
guide.s6.l6: Emergency numbers such as 119 or 112 can have a place of their own.
guide.s6.l7: On first launch it looks through the contacts for people saved as "eldest daughter" or "husband" and puts them in place for you.
guide.s6.p1: 88Phone does not change your settings. It is a phone app with nothing left but calling. There is no contact list. The screen shows big photos and big names of the people they call most, and one tap on a card makes the call.
guide.s6.p2: There are no ads. Nobody taps an ad by mistake while trying to make a call. Neither contacts nor call history ever leave the phone. There is no sign-up either.
guide.title: How to enlarge the text on a parent's phone — what settings can and cannot do

p88.desc: A phone app with nothing left but calling. Tap a photo and the call goes through. Your parents do not need to learn anything new. Android · Free.
p88.faq.1.a: Yes. Install it and use it right away. For free you get four people you call most as big photo cards, and you can both call and text. There are no ads, even in the free version.
p88.faq.2.a: Pay 8,800원 once and the places grow from four to practically unlimited, and the text messages from 4 to 16. You can also edit the messages yourself. You pay once, not every month. There are no ads either way.
p88.faq.3.a: No. 88Phone has no server. Contacts are read only on the phone and never sent anywhere.
p88.faq.3.q: Does the company take my parents' contacts?
p88.faq.4.a: For now it runs on Android only.
p88.faq.5.a: No, never. When you turn on "Show who called", Android asks for call screening permission, but 88Phone only notes the number; it never blocks or rejects a call. If you leave it off, calls work as usual.
p88.faq.6.a: It is best if a son or daughter helps the first time. There are only three choices to make: the screen language and text size, the family members to put in place, and the four text messages they use most. After that your parent only taps photos.
p88.faq.6.q: Can an older parent install and set it up alone?
p88.faq.lead: Ways to enlarge text using only the phone's settings are collected in How to enlarge the text on a parent's phone.
p88.feat.contacts.alt: The picture chooser. Pictures of people and everyday pictures such as hospital, pharmacy, taxi and bank.
p88.feat.contacts.h3: It uses the contacts already on the phone
p88.feat.contacts.p1: Nothing is stored separately and nothing is sent out. There is no server. Change a number in Contacts and it changes in 88Phone too.
p88.feat.contacts.p2: On first launch it looks through the contacts and finds the people saved as "eldest daughter" or "husband" and shows them to you. You just pick the ones to add. Photos can be taken on the spot or chosen from the album, and anyone without a photo gets one of 18 pictures such as hospital, pharmacy or taxi.
p88.feat.face.alt: The 88Phone home screen. Wooden cards with a name and a big photo, arranged in four places.
p88.feat.face.h3: Tap a face, not a name
p88.feat.face.p1: No scrolling through a list of names. The photo fills half the card, so even without reading you know who is who. Just put the people they call most in place. For free you get four; pay once and a new row is added every time the places fill up, so there is practically no limit.
p88.feat.keypad.alt: The keypad screen. A large keypad and the number shown in groups like 010-1234-5678.
p88.feat.keypad.h3: Numbers not on a card, by hand
p88.feat.keypad.p1: The keypad is big. The number you type fills a whole line and is shown in groups, like 010-1234-5678.
p88.feat.keypad.p2: Emergency numbers such as 119 or 112 can have a card of their own. Pick the right number for the country you live in.
p88.feat.lang.alt: The first-launch screen. Choose from 14 languages including 한국어, English, 日本語 and 中文.
p88.feat.lang.p1: Korean, English, Japanese, Chinese, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Hindi, Portuguese, Russian, Vietnamese, Thai and Indonesian. Choose on first launch and change it any time in Settings.
p88.feat.lang.p2: For families who speak different languages, or for parents living abroad. The ready-made text messages come in that language too.
p88.feat.sms.alt: The text message chooser. Common phrases such as "Please call me" and "I love you" as big buttons.
p88.feat.sms.p1: No typing. Pick from everyday phrases like "Please call me", "I love you" or "Good night" and the message fills itself in. The ones used most rise to the top by themselves. You get 4 for free and 16 after a one-time payment, and you can edit them yourself.
p88.feat.size.alt: The settings screen. Choose a button style (wood, porcelain, black, rubber), how many cards per row, and screen brightness.
p88.feat.size.h3: Not just the text gets bigger
p88.feat.size.p1: Increase the size and the photos and cards grow with it. There are five sizes: normal, large, larger, very large and fit to screen, and it starts on "larger". Reduce the cards per row to one and everything is bigger still, or hide the photos and show only very large names.
p88.feat.size.p2: Photos can be square or round, and the buttons come in four styles: wood, porcelain, black and rubber. Screen brightness can follow the phone or stay always light or always dark.
p88.feat.tap.alt: The enlarged card that appears when a photo is tapped. Below the name and number are a green Call button and a blue Text button.
p88.feat.tap.p1: Tap the card and the call goes through. One tap is all it takes. If you would like one extra step, turn off "Call on tap" in Settings. The card then enlarges first and offers a choice between calling and texting. Press and hold a card to move it or remove it.
p88.feat.lead: There are only three screens for making a call: home, the enlarged card, and the keypad.
p88.get.h2b: Install it on your parent's phone
p88.get.p: Open the phone's camera and point it at the QR code on the left; an address appears on the screen. Tap it once and the install screen opens.
p88.get.soonP: It is not on Google Play yet. Once it is listed, the button and QR code below will lead to the install screen.

p88.ogDesc: A phone app with nothing left but calling. Your parents do not need to learn anything new.
p88.price.c1: Pay once and keep using it. It is not money that leaves your account every month.
p88.price.c2: Without paying anything, you still get four people in place and can call and text as usual.
p88.price.lead: The app is free. Calling works the same whether you pay or not.
p88.ring.h2: A mark stays on whoever called
p88.ring.p: The card of someone who called you gets a mark and its border blinks. It works only after you turn it on in Settings. 88Phone only notes the number; it never blocks or rejects a call.
p88.story.h2b: To sons, daughters, grandsons and granddaughters everywhere
p88.story.lead: 88Phone was not planned as a product. It was made to put on a grandmother's phone.
p88.story.p1: Grandmother's eyes kept getting worse. One day she stopped making calls and only answered them. She could not read the small text on the screen, so she could not find who was who in the contacts.
p88.story.p2: We turned the font size in the phone's settings all the way up. We turned on screen zoom too. She still said "I still can't see it." Only the letters had grown; there were still hundreds of names to search, and the bigger the text, the fewer names fit on one screen. Long names were cut off in the middle, which made them even harder to recognise.
p88.story.p3: She had a smartphone, but the only thing she actually used was the phone. Not the maps, not the photo album. Because that one thing was hard, the whole phone had become a difficult object.
p88.story.p4: So we made an app with nothing left but calling. We removed the contact list. The screen holds only big photos and big names of family. If there is nothing to search for, there is nothing to fail to find. Tap, and it calls.
p88.story.p5: Now she says "the letters are big, I can see them." And she calls first. That is all we wanted.
p88.story.p6: If your grandparents rarely call, it may not be that they do not want to; it may be that calling is hard. Everyone's eyesight fades, but losing the ability to make a call should not be part of it.
p88.story.p7: Install 88Phone on your grandparents' phone and put the people they call most in place. It takes five minutes during a holiday or weekend visit. After that, they only tap photos.
p88.story.p8: That is also why it works in 14 languages. Fading eyesight knows no borders.

priv.desc: 88Phone privacy policy. 88Phone collects no personal data and has no server.
priv.note: This is an English translation provided for reference. The Korean original is the authoritative text.
priv.s1.p1: 88Phone collects no personal data. 88Phone has no server and never transmits or stores any user information outside the device.
priv.s2.h2: 2. Information the app uses on the device
priv.s2.l1: Contacts (optional) — used to show the name, phone number and photo of the people you place on the screen. The app keeps only the contact identifier and the last name and number it saw, in the device's internal storage. If you do not grant it, you can still pick people one at a time through the phone's own contacts screen.
priv.s2.l2: Phone (optional) — used only to place a call when you press [Call]. If you do not grant it, the app only enters the number into the phone app and you press the call button yourself.
priv.s2.l3: Call screening role (optional) — only if you turn it on yourself, the incoming number is recorded on the device so that the matching contact can be shown on screen. It never blocks or rejects calls and never records call content.
priv.s2.l4: Photos (optional) — when you take a photo for a card or choose one from the album, the single chosen photo is reduced in size and saved only in the app's folder. The phone's contact photos are not changed and the whole album is not read.
priv.s2.l5: Installed app list (optional) — only when you use 88Phone as your home screen, the app reads app names and icons to show a list for switching to other apps. It is neither stored nor transmitted.
priv.s2.l6: Text messages — 88Phone does not send messages itself. It only enters the chosen sentence into the phone's messaging app, and you press send. It therefore does not request the SMS permission.
priv.s2.p1: 88Phone reads and uses the following information only on your device.
priv.s2.p2: None of this information leaves the device. It is deleted together with the app.
priv.s3.p1: So that the people you placed and your settings are restored when you change phones or reinstall the app, it uses Android's automatic backup. Backup data is stored in your own Google account backup space, and we cannot access it. You can turn backup off in the phone's settings.
priv.s4.p1: 88Phone has no ads. It shows no advertising, does not read the advertising identifier and uses no analytics tools.
priv.s5.p1: The payment that unlocks more contacts and messages is made through Google Play, and payment details are handled by Google. We do not collect or keep any payment information. See Google's privacy policy at policies.google.com/privacy.
priv.s6.p1: Because all information stays on your device, you can view, change and delete it yourself. To remove a person, tap their card and then the trash icon; to erase everything, use phone Settings > Apps > 88Phone > Storage > Clear data. Permissions can be withdrawn in the Permissions menu on the same screen.
priv.s7.p1: 88Phone is not aimed at children and does not knowingly collect children's personal data.
priv.s9.p1: If this policy changes, the changes and their effective date will be posted on this page.
priv.title: 88Phone Privacy Policy
